author: Ash

copy.intro: The tee you wanted at Tillys is gone in your size, or there's no Tillys within a sensible drive. These are the stores and labels people go to instead for skate, surf and streetwear basics. Multi-brand mall stores built like Tillys come first, then the brands you'd shop for the same reasons. Men's is Tillys' biggest department, so every price here is for men's T-shirts, next to its own $29.99 to $45.

bodies.zumiez:
Zumiez is the closest thing to another Tillys. It's a multi-brand mall chain for skate, snow and streetwear, and its tees start with the Shaka Wear Max Heavyweight T-Shirt ($24.99).

The two even share a collab: the Santa Cruz x Pokémon Power Dot tee is $31.95 here and $31.99 at Tillys. Zumiez reaches higher at the top, up to the Affliction Theory Rhinestone T-Shirt ($64.95), so it's the better bet for the louder brands. Free shipping starts at $64.94, a few dollars under Tillys' $70. Returns get 30 days, and taking one back to a store is free, while mailed returns pay their own postage.

The catch is sizing. Its tees mostly run XS to 3XL, so if you need a 4XL or 5XL, Hot Topic goes further.
bodies.pacsun:
PacSun is the pick if you want Tillys' California surf roots with more of a denim focus. It started as a surf shop in Seal Beach, and today it's best known for baggy jeans, hoodies and men's graphic tees.

Its shipping rule saves you money. US orders over $59 ship free, and so does any order with jeans or pants in it, whatever the total. That's a lower bar than Tillys' $70, so a single pair of jeans and a tee cost nothing to send. Like Tillys, it sells its own label next to other brands, so you can still mix names in one basket.

It ships within the US only, the same as Tillys right now. If you're ordering from Canada, Volcom ships there at its US rates.
bodies.hot-topic:
Hot Topic is where to go when the tee you want has a band, a game or an anime on it. It's a pop-culture merch and clothing store, and its men's tees run from $12.99 to $50.90, so it starts well under Tillys' cheapest.

Go for the sizes. Tees go from XS to 5XL, plus a tall run from LT to 4XLT, which only Old Navy also covers among these picks. The Shaka Wear 7.5 Oz. Heavyweight T-Shirt ($15.90) is the plain option if you only need blanks. Free shipping starts at $75, and returns get 30 days in a store or by mail.

Watch the pre-orders, though. Pre-order merch shipped to your home adds $1.99 an item, and choosing ship-to-store waives it.
bodies.aeropostale:
Aeropostale is the easy-shipping choice for the same mall-store basics: graphic tees, baggy jeans and hoodies, all under its own name. Free US shipping starts at $25, the lowest bar of any store here.

It's a single brand, so you're buying Aero and nothing else, where Tillys mixes in Volcom, Vans and the rest. Start with the men's graphic tees and the jeans, which come in baggy, mega baggy and super baggy fits. Men's waists run 26 to 46, and the XXL and XXXL sizes are online only, so order those rather than hunting in a store.

Much of the range shows a Comp. Value above a lower price, and the lower one is what you pay. If you want brand-name skate labels instead of one house brand, Zumiez or PacSun fit better.
bodies.volcom:
Volcom is the way to buy one of Tillys' own brands straight from the source. Tillys stocks it, and Volcom's site sells men's short-sleeve tees from $22 for the Workwear Short Sleeve Tee up to $42.

It's been a skate, surf and snowboard label since 1991, so the tees lean on artwork. The Featured Artist line, like the Daniel Shepard Walleye Short Sleeve Tee ($40), sits at the top of the range. More than half the tees carry a markdown, so check the sale section before paying full price.

It also ships to Canada at its US rates, free over $99, which Tillys can't do right now. Returns get 30 days with a prepaid label. A refund to your card costs $7, but a gift card costs nothing.
bodies.forever-21:
Forever 21 is the cheapest way here to stock up on plain tees. Its 100% Cotton Crew Tee ($7.99) costs about a quarter of Tillys' cheapest, and the basic crews and V-necks run XS to XXXL.

It's online only now, after closing its US stores, so there's nowhere to try anything on. Graphic tees top out with the Velour Rhinestone Short Sleeve T-Shirt ($34.99), still well under Tillys' top price. Shipping is free over $50, and returns get 30 days, with a $9.99 fee taken off and no returns at all on clearance or final sale.

It's a trend store for everyone, though, so for the skate and surf names Tillys carries, Zumiez is closer.
bodies.cotton-on:
Cotton On is the budget basics pick with the most relaxed returns. The Easy T-Shirt ($7) is the cheapest tee on this page, and the Fitted Henley T-Shirt ($34.99) tops its men's range. Four Easy T-Shirts cost less than one Tillys tee.

Returns have no time limit. Eligible items in original condition can go back whenever, with proof of purchase, and return shipping within the US is free. Tillys gives you 30 days and charges $6.95 for a mailed return. Free delivery starts at $75.

It's an Australian brand with one label, and plenty of the men's range sits on markdown. If you want graphic tees with a skate name on them, Neff or Volcom fit better.
bodies.neff-headwear:
Neff sells graphic tees at one flat price. Nearly every men's tee costs $21.98, about $8 under Tillys' cheapest, and that includes the Garfield collab, like the Men's NEFF X Garfield Ballin T-Shirt ($21.98).

It started as snow and skate headwear, so the beanies are worth adding to the order. It's based in Irvine, California, the same city as Tillys' headquarters. Shipping is free over $50, and returns get 45 days with return shipping paid, which is longer and cheaper than Tillys' 30 days and $6.95 fee.

Sizes stop at 2XL, though, and it only ships within the US. For anything bigger, Hot Topic and Tillys both go to 5XL.
bodies.vans:
Go to Vans if your Tillys trip is mostly about the shoes and the tees that go with them. It calls itself the original action sports footwear company, founded in 1966, and it makes youth-culture apparel alongside the sneakers. Tillys stocks it too.

Vans runs its own stores and dealers across the US, like the Vans Store at Westfield Century City in Los Angeles. That puts the whole range in one place, more than any multi-brand shop's slice. Its store locator lists stores and dealers state by state. It's owned by VF Corporation.

If you'd rather have Vans next to other skate brands in one basket, Zumiez or Tillys itself is the better trip.
bodies.american-eagle:
American Eagle gives you 60 days to return jeans-and-tee basics for a full refund, twice Tillys' 30. An online return costs $5.

It's a single brand, like Aeropostale, and its men's T-shirts lean plain: logo tees, lived-in basics and graphics like Snoopy and Ford. Free US shipping starts at $75, and under that it's $7.95. AE.com also carries additional sizes and styles, so look there if a store runs out.

Most men's tees carry a markdown, such as the AE Standard Fit Lived-In T-Shirt at $11.99 against a $19.95 list price. So it can undercut Tillys while a deal runs, but there's no skate or surf label in the mix. For those, PacSun is the closer mall store.
bodies.old-navy:
Old Navy works when you're shopping for the whole family as well as yourself. It's Gap Inc.'s value brand, with stores in 49 states plus DC and Puerto Rico, and it carries big and tall sizes for adults and extended sizes for kids.

Every order gets free returns within 30 days, by prepaid label or in a store, and Premier members get up to 45. Rewards members get free shipping over $50, and the bag combines with Gap, Athleta and Banana Republic.

It's the furthest from Tillys in style. There's no skate or surf brand here, so treat it as the basics run and go to Zumiez or PacSun for the labels.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body: Start with what you're replacing. For the same mix of skate and surf brands under one roof, Zumiez is the closest, and PacSun is the one if jeans are on the list, since they ship free. Need a 4XL, a 5XL or a tall? Hot Topic. For the brands Tillys itself sells, go to Volcom or Vans directly. On a tight budget, Cotton On and Forever 21 have tees under $10, and Neff keeps graphic tees near $22 with free returns. American Eagle and Old Navy are the safe calls for plain basics with easy returns. And if you're in Canada, Volcom ships there at its US rates.

faqs.a: A Southern California chain for casual clothes, shoes and accessories rooted in surf and skate. It opened in 1982 as World of Jeans and Tops, now has stores in more than 30 states, and sells brands like Volcom and Vans next to its own RSQ label.
It's a public company, Tillys, Inc., listed on the New York Stock Exchange as TLYS and based in Irvine, California. Hezy Shaked and Tilly Levine founded it in 1982.
You get 30 days from the order date or the store purchase date. A mailed return costs $6.95 for the label, but taking an online order back to a Tillys store is free.
